record.paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
record.original_question: For the asynchronous deterministic shared-memory Write-All problem with p processors and t memory locations under adversarial failures or delays, is it possible to achieve optimal total work O(t) while using p = t^delta processors for some delta greater than 1/2?

evidence.quote: Next observe that an optimal algorithm for Write-All must have work Theta(t).
Our second and final open problem is as follows: Is it possible to solve the asynchronous Write-All problem with optimal work O(t) using the number of processors p = t^delta for delta > 1/2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The asynchronous deterministic Write-All problem is defined as follows. There are $t$ shared memory locations, each initialized to $0$, and $p$ asynchronous processors operating on this shared memory. The processors execute a common deterministic algorithm and must cooperate so that every one of the $t$ memory locations is set to $1$ at least once before the algorithm terminates. Processors are subject to an adversary that may impose arbitrary asynchrony (including delays, halting, or crash failures of any subset of processors), provided that at least one processor remains live until termination. The total work of an execution is the sum, over all processors, of the number of basic shared-memory steps each processor performs while still active; the worst-case work of an algorithm is the maximum of this quantity over all admissible adversarial schedules. An algorithm is called work-optimal if its worst-case total work is $O(t)$.

Question: Does there exist a constant $\delta > 1/2$ and a deterministic algorithm solving the asynchronous Write-All problem with $t$ memory locations and $p = t^{\delta}$ processors whose total work is $O(t)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Known deterministic asynchronous Write-All algorithms achieve work-optimal $O(t)$ only for processor counts well below $t^{1/2}$. Kowalski–Shvartsman obtained work optimality for $p = O(t^{1/(2+\varepsilon)})$, and later improvements still stay below the $t^{1/2}$ threshold (e.g. $p = O((t/\log t)^{1/(3+\varepsilon)})$). No deterministic work-optimal algorithm is known for any $\delta > 1/2$, and the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Work-Optimal Deterministic Algorithm for the Certified Write-All Problem with a Nontrivial Number of Asynchronous Processors
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm with work complexity O(n + p^(2+ε)), achieving work optimality for p = O(n^(1/(2+ε)))
status_evidence.claim: Best previously known work-optimal range stays strictly below p = t^{1/2}.

status_evidence.title: Writing-all deterministically and optimally using a nontrivial number of asynchronous processors
status_evidence.snippet: Work optimal for m = O((n/log n)^{1/(3+ε)})
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent improvements remain below the t^{1/2} barrier, indicating the δ > 1/2 question is still open.
